CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough for one week with worsening symptoms over the last two days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Billy is a 74-year-old patient presenting with a cough that started approximately one week ago. He reports initially having a dry cough that has progressed to productive cough with yellow sputum. He notes feeling unwell for the past two days. He denies fever but reports feeling warm. He denies chills but describes occasional achiness. He denies shortness of breath. He reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and mild sinus pressure bilaterally. He notes no sick contacts in his household. Additionally, the patient reports that while coughing earlier today, he fell down approximately four to five stairs, twisting his right knee. He has been able to walk since the fall but with a slight limp and pain primarily on the inner aspect of the knee. The right knee pain has not improved with rest. He has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold symptoms with minimal improvement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for productive cough with yellow sputum, nasal congestion, postnasal drainage, and sinus pressure. Denies fever, chills, shortness of breath. Reports mild achiness. Positive for right knee pain and mild limp after fall today.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
3. Dayquil over-the-counter (as needed for cough and cold)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a teacher. Denies tobacco and alcohol use during this visit. Patient is married. Lives with wife.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood pressure 125/62 mmHg, Heart rate in the 80s, Oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
General: No acute distress.
HEENT: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses. Nasal exam shows erythema and edema of bilateral nasal turbinates with yellow discharge. Uvula midline. No erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space.
Neck: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy noted.
Lungs: Coarse rhonchi bilaterally that clears with cough.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated.
Knee: Right knee with pain to palpation, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to right medial knee, no effusion.

RESULTS
Pending: Lipid panel, hemoglobin A1c, right knee X-ray.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection with mild bronchitis: Continue supportive care and over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to help mobilize secretions. No antibiotics at this time. Patient instructed to call if symptoms worsen; will consider chest X-ray if pneumonia suspected.
2. Right medial collateral ligament strain from fall: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening exercises. Order right knee X-ray to rule out bony injury.
3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel for monitoring.
4. Diabetes mellitus: Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1c to assess glycemic control and need for medication adjustment. Strongly encouraged patient to monitor dietary sugar intake and report blood glucose readings through patient portal to optimize long-term health outcomes.
